source_notes.label: A quantified solvothermal preparation
source_notes.summary: The main route uses 7 mmol CuCl2·2H2O and 4 mmol Te in ethylenediamine. The solvent fills 85% of a 100 mL Teflon-lined autoclave before the two solids are added successively. A sealed 160 °C treatment for 10 h, natural cooling, filtration, water/ethanol washing and vacuum drying at 60 °C for 4 h produce the specimen characterized in Figures 1–3.

source_notes.label: Phase, crystallite size and particle diameter
source_notes.summary: Figure 1 indexes hexagonal Cu7Te4 with a = 8.335 Å and c = 7.211 Å, close to JCPDS 18-456. The source estimates a crystallite size of about 15 nm by the Scherrer formula. Figure 3 separately shows homogeneous nanoparticles with an average TEM diameter near 15 nm. These two approximate estimates use different methods and do not establish a measured coordinate model or a particle-size distribution.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 1 and 3 and accompanying analysis

source_notes.label: XPS composition and a printed unit anomaly
source_notes.summary: The reported Cu 2p and Te 3d peak positions are 932.4 eV and 572.7 eV. Peak quantification gives Cu:Te = 63.41:36.29; this ratio is retained without renormalization. The printed charge reference is C 1s at 284.60 kV, although specimen peaks and plotted axes use eV. That unit anomaly remains unresolved. The source reports no obvious oxide peaks but provides no impurity detection limit.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figure 2 and XPS discussion

source_notes.label: Solvent comparisons and author-proposed mechanism
source_notes.summary: Benzene and diethylamine comparisons did not react tellurium with copper chloride. The authors propose that polar, bidentate ethylenediamine stabilizes metal-polytellurido intermediates and promotes dissolution, diffusion and crystallization while absorbing reaction heat. They compare quoted solvent critical temperatures of 318 °C for ethylenediamine and 374 °C for water. These are explanatory source context, not measured synthesis temperatures or identified intermediates.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3, Solvent and reaction-mechanism discussion

source_notes.label: Feed-ratio and precursor comparisons
source_notes.summary: A 3:2 copper-salt/Te feed gives Cu7Te4 mixed with unreacted tellurium rather than the expected Cu3Te2. A 2:1 feed gives only hexagonal Cu7Te4 rather than Cu2Te. Replacing CuCl2 with CuI also gives Cu7Te4 nanoparticles. The source does not separately assign absolute charges, complete conditions, particle sizes or displayed figures to these comparisons; they remain supporting contexts.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3, Molar-ratio and CuI substitution paragraph

source_notes.label: An unresolved intermediate and further heating
source_notes.summary: At 140 °C an XRD-observed intermediate could not be identified against the available JCPDS patterns. Its assignment as a Cu/Te/ethylenediamine complex is the authors’ inference. Further heating of this intermediate at 180 °C produces Cu7Te4 described as pure, with no treatment time or numerical purity limit supplied. Below 120 °C, neither the intermediate nor reacted tellurium is reported. The 180 °C context retains explicit lineage from the 140 °C intermediate without inventing its formula or handling.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3, Temperature-dependent intermediate discussion

source_notes.label: Application motivation is not a measured property
source_notes.summary: The introduction discusses thermoelectric applications, thermopower, electrical resistivity and thermal conductivity using cited literature. No numerical thermoelectric property is measured on these Cu7Te4 powders. Cited full papers remain unreviewed and do not supply missing experimental conditions.
